title: Release notes in the app, trade unit overlap on saved lists
summary: A short note on what changed after each release, and a way to spot producers a saved list is hiding.

items.text: After each release the app tells you what changed. The notice appears once, and you can reopen it any time from the What's New row in your profile menu.
Your profile menu now shows which release and build you are running. Include that line when you report a problem and we can tell exactly which version you were on.
A saved list now shows which of its producers fall outside your current trade unit selection, so you can see at a glance why a list looks shorter than you expected.
The activity status column no longer shows stale values for originators who have signed in recently.

title: Shared recap groups and crop lists that match your trade units
summary: Recap groups can be edited by more than their creator, and crop dropdowns now reflect the trade units you work in.

items.text: A recap group is no longer editable only by the person who made it, so a team can keep a shared group current without going through one owner.
Crop dropdowns show the commodities that belong to your trade units, so specialty and organic crops appear for the people who trade them and stay out of everyone else's way.

title: A cleaner Bid Sheet print view and a layout built for laptops

items.text: The print view was rebuilt to fit the page first: it sizes itself to the columns you actually use and drops empty ones instead of stretching them across the sheet.
The daily layout and commodity colours were reworked so the sheet stays readable at a glance.
Screens now adapt to laptop-width displays rather than assuming a large monitor, so less is squeezed or cut off.
Your profile menu links straight to the Trade Unit Preferences app, and your groups refresh here as soon as you close it.

title: Mention a group in a note

items.text: Typing @ in a note offers your Daily Recap groups as well as individual people, so one mention reaches everyone in the group.
A producer can carry more than one contact, with a primary contact shown on the profile.
Bushel conversions now use each commodity's own weight rather than a single shared factor.
